{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c45c7d51678efb6896566520c26168b9d82d50da76944af5e1ac18dbb606e56c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions","heading":"C — Emergency parking, where parking is illegal, entering and exiting freeways and highways, lane use, the gore area, stopping on the freeway, HOV lanes, other freeway restrictions and highway driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Emergency parking, where parking is illegal, entering and exiting freeways and highways, lane use, the gore area, stopping on the freeway, HOV lanes, other freeway restrictions and highway driving
Knowledge domain: what to do when you must leave a vehicle on a road, the list of places where parking is illegal with its distances, how to merge onto and leave a freeway, which lane to use, what a gore area is, how to get help on a freeway, and the HOV and other freeway restrictions.

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
If you must leave your vehicle on a highway or street, pull onto the shoulder as far from traffic as you can, or as close to the curb as possible where there is one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Before leaving it, set the parking brake, shift into park or leave a manual transmission in gear, and switch off the engine. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Put out proper emergency signals and, if possible, stay with the vehicle until help arrives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
If you have to walk away from the vehicle, lock it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Parking is illegal on a sidewalk, in front of any public or private driveway, and inside the boundaries of an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Parking is illegal on a crosswalk, and also anywhere closer than 20 feet to a crosswalk at an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Parking on any freeway or interstate highway is illegal except in an emergency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
You may not park where signs prohibit it or in any way that creates a hazard for other vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Parking within 50 feet of a railroad crossing is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
You may not park on a bridge or inside a tunnel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
Freeways and interstate highways are built to carry higher-speed traffic safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Drivers entering a freeway must yield to the traffic already on it and are responsible for merging safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A01
To merge, match your speed to the traffic in the freeway's right lane, signal, check the traffic around you and merge carefully once it is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A01
While entering a freeway, do not cross a solid line or drive through a gore area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A01
Signal before you exit a freeway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A01
Most freeways have deceleration lanes to help you exit, and proper braking gives a smooth exit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A01
When exiting in heavy traffic, keep a space cushion behind the vehicle ahead and do not cross a solid line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A01
A divided highway or freeway has separate roadways for the two directions, often with several lanes on each side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Some highways meet other roads at traffic signals, while controlled-access highways have no signals or intersections and are entered and left only by ramps; these are called expressways or freeways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
Get into the proper lane well in advance so you can enter or leave the highway safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
Signal your exit before you reach the exit ramp. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
When joining a highway, yield to drivers already on it and speed up to match their speed as you enter the travel lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
If you miss your exit, do not stop and never back up; leave at the next exit and follow the signs to rejoin the road going the other way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
On any road with two or more lanes, drive on the right half except when passing or when signs say otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
On highways with three or more lanes in one direction, the right lane usually serves entering and exiting traffic, so it may move slower or faster than the other lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
At rush hour, drivers who are not exiting may want to stay out of the right lane to leave room for vehicles entering and leaving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
Watch for vehicles merging into your lane, signal your own lane changes, keep within posted speed limits and do not tailgate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A02
Driving over or parking on any part of a gore area, the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp, is against the law. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A02
If you need help on a freeway, pull as far as you can onto the right shoulder and avoid stopping on or near the ramps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A02
To signal for help, turn on your emergency flashers or raise the hood; after dark, switch on the inside dome light or set out flares or portable warning signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A02
Wait for help with your vehicle and do not walk along the freeway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A02
When you come upon a disabled vehicle on the freeway, slow down, move over and pass around it with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A03
HOV lanes are marked by white diamonds painted in the roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A03
At the posted times on weekdays, a vehicle carrying fewer than two persons, counting the driver, may not use an HOV lane, which is then reserved for car pools, motorcycles and buses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A03
A motorist who breaks the HOV restriction faces substantial fines and penalties. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A03
Always signal and take care when crossing the solid white line into or out of an HOV lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A03
On a freeway, never drive over or across a median or divided-highway separation, and never make a U-turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A03
On a freeway, never change lanes without signaling, and get onto the freeway only by an on-ramp. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A03
Do not park or stop on a freeway except in areas provided for it; parking on the shoulder is banned except in an emergency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A03
If you miss a freeway exit, do not back up; you must go on to the next exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F42 | anchor: A03
Before highway driving, make sure your vehicle is in good operating condition and can keep up highway speeds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F43 | anchor: A03
Keep right and use the left lane only to pass; on a three-lane highway, treat the far right lane as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F44 | anchor: A03
Drive in the middle of your lane between the lines, and use your rearview mirror and turn signals when changing lanes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F45 | anchor: A03
Traffic is controlled by signal lights, traffic signs and pavement markings, and you must fully understand them to drive safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

Misconceptions: missing an exit never justifies stopping or backing up, you always continue to the next exit; the entering driver, not freeway traffic, is responsible for a safe merge; the fire hydrant, crosswalk and railroad parking distances are three different numbers; the HOV restriction applies at the posted times, not around the clock.
Mnemonics: Hydrant, crosswalk, railroad — small, middle, large; on the freeway, miss it and move on.
Glossary: gore area means the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp; deceleration lane means an exit lane where you slow down off the main road; controlled access means a highway entered and left only by ramps; HOV lane means a high-occupancy-vehicle lane marked by white diamonds.
Dynamic facts: HOV hours are set by posted signs that can change, and the manual does not state HOV fine amounts, so check the signs and current Arizona law.
